Park and Recreation Commission

  Inglewood, California
  February 6, 2025

The Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission meeting was convened in the Council Chambers
located on the ninth floor of City Hall on February 6, 2025. Commissioner Denmon called the
meeting to order at 6:02 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Stephanie Maldonado announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Commissioner Lee Denmon - District 1, Commissioner Octavio Padilla -
  District 2, Commissioner Henry Brown - Commissioner at Large
  Absent:  Commissioner Cynthia McLemore - District 3, Commissioner Christopher
  Beck - District 4

City Personnel present for the meeting were as follows:

  Thomas Uwal  Director of Parks, Recreation, and Community Service Department
  Brian McClure  Parks Administration Superintendent
  Baz Devlia  Human Services Superintendent
  Anthony Harris  Recreation Supervisor
  Stephanie Maldonado  Senior Management Assistant

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None.

MINUTES. It was moved by Commissioner Brown and second by Commissioner Padilla that
the minutes for the Park and Recreation Commission meeting held on June 6, 2024, be
approved. The following roll call vote carried the motion:
Ayes: Commissioners Brown, Padilla, and Denmon
Noes: None

It was moved by Commissioner Brown and second by Commissioner Padilla that the
minutes for the Park and Recreation Commission meeting held on October 3, 2024, be
approved. The following roll call vote carried the motion:
Ayes: Commissioners Brown, Padilla, and Denmon
Noes: None

It was moved by Commissioner Padilla and second by Commissioner Denmon that the
minutes for the Park and Recreation Commission meeting held on November 7, 2024, be
approved. The following roll call vote carried the motion:
Ayes: Commissioners Brown, Padilla, and Denmon
Noes: None

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission

DIRECTOR’S BUSINESS.

REPORT - PARKS ADMINISTRATION. Parks Administration Superintendent Brian McClure reported
the following: Park Maintenance – Century Boulevard Planting Project – Park staff are adding
plants and mulch to all the medians on Century Blvd. Tree Maintenance – The City’s urban forest
contains over 17,000 trees. In the first quarter, we have trimmed 1,516 trees and planted 41. We
have grounded 40 stumps and removed one tree. The urban forest has over 200 species of trees
with the two most popular being the Southern Magnolia and the Indian Laurel fig. Graffiti
Abatement – Shared photos of Jose Gonzalez and Emmanuel Raines removing graffiti. In the first
quarter of our fiscal year, staff removed 1,660 tags in October, 1,035 in November, and 442 in
December. We removed the following amount of graffiti tags in each district: District 1: 487,
District 2: 1,331, District 3: 772, and District 4: 547. The Graffiti hotline is (310) 412-8739.

REPORT - RECREATION. Recreation Supervisor Anthony Harris reported the following: Black
History Celebration – The city’s 3rd annual Black History Celebration will be held on Saturday,
February 22nd in downtown Inglewood, along Market Street, from 11:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. The
event will feature an exciting lineup of live entertainment, including performances by Biscuits and
Gravy, Erin Stevenson, DJ QwessCoast, Spirit of Oya, India Shawn, Iman Europe, and Charlie Bereal,
to name a few. Other activities include arts and crafts, art exhibitions, health screenings,
informational, commercial, and food vendors. A key highlight of the event will be the speech
contest, where the winners will showcase their dynamic and inspiring speeches. We invite you to
join us for this special occasion and encourage you to extend an invitation to your friends, family,
and neighbors. Health Workshops – The Parks, Recreation and Community Services Department,
in partnership with Youthful Joy Foundation, will offer a series of FREE health workshops for the
community. Classes will take place at Rogers Park on Saturdays from 11:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. The
first Caregiver Cooking workshop will take place on Saturday, February 22nd. This class is designed
to engage parents and promote healthy eating habits both at home and in the community. We
encourage all individuals interested in learning how to prepare nutritious meals and foster healthy
eating practices within their households to attend this informative and interactive workshop. IYSL
– Website Tour, Basketball, and Soccer –- The Inglewood Youth Sports League continues to thrive
bringing sports programming to the community. The IYSL is a high functioning and trailblazing
program led by volunteers and a talented Citywide Youth Sports staff. The winter season brings
basketball and soccer with both programs showing tremendous growth in 2025. The soccer league
still seeking a community partner began in 2022 with 56 participants. Today the program boast
217 participants with girls and boys ages 4 – 12. Teams practice once a week and play games on
Saturday’s at Champions Field. The Inglewood Youth Basketball League is sponsored by the Los
Angeles Clippers and has grown from 175 participants just after COVID to 354 players in 2025. The
action in the 4-5 year old division is more adorable than Sports Center highlights worthy. However,
the experience of learning fundamental skills, and having fun is most important. The fast pace
action begins to take flight as the age groups reach 8 to 14 years old. The City of Inglewood is rich
with talent and will resume play in the SCMAF (Southern California Municipal Athletic Federation)
tournament in 2025. This is where municipal programs from the bay area to San Diego compete
over a weekend in a pool play format. Inglewood is poised to return to the top in this tournament
in 2025. Come out and watch these young people dribble, pass, and shoot on Thursday evenings
and all day on Saturday’s at Rogers and Darby Parks. You won’t be disappointed. Both winter

  2
   Park and Recreation Commission

season leagues will conclude on consecutive weekends in April as basketball plays its
Championship tournament at the Intuit Dome and Soccer host their title games in prime time at
Champions Field. Both seasons will conclude with awards and soul food from DD’s Catfish and
Chicken truck. For more information on our Inglewood Youth Sports Leagues, visit our city sports
website at: https://cityofinglewood.leagueapps.com/

REPORT - HUMAN SERVICES. Human Services Superintendent Baz Devlia reported the following:
Senior Center Operations – Our Senior Center is packed with more seniors than ever as we continue
to grow our participation numbers, as well as increase our offerings. For February, we have
presentations by Grace Farwell of Helping Elderly Live Productively, or H.E.L.P. for short. On
February 7th, Grace will be presenting on the topic of choosing an emergency alert system. On
February 21st, the topic will be Dementia 101 / Communicating & Caring for People with Dementia.
We have Mercedes Aguirre from the Los Angeles County Department of Mental Health presenting
a session on Depression & Anxiety on February 10th. Also starting on February 10th is our
collaboration with the American Association of Retired Persons, better known as AARP, who will
provide free tax preparation services to our seniors every other Tuesday through March 24, 2025.
On Friday, February 14, 2025, we are encouraging staff and seniors to wear red for our Valentine’s
Day events, which are from 10:30 a.m. to 11:00 a.m., where seniors will receive a little treat and
enjoy some poetry reading. On February 19th, we have a program to honor Black History Month
from 10:30 a.m. to 11:30 a.m. The event will include a special performance by our Inspirational
Choir, a fashion show, and poetry reading. Senior Nutrition – We serve approximately 450 seniors
weekly through home-delivered meals for homebound seniors and congregate meals at our Senior
Center. We continue to provide fresh produce weekly in collaboration with the Social Justice
Learning Institute and monthly shelf-stable meal boxes in collaboration with the Los Angeles Food
Bank. Child and Adult Care Food Program – The Child and Adult Care Food Program, informally
CACFP, serves meals to youth 18 years old and under and operates at Crenshaw Library, Rogers
Park, and Darby Park. The program's hours are Monday through Friday, providing supper from 2:30
p.m. - 3:30 p.m. and snacks from 4:30 p.m. - 5:00 p.m. We serve an average of 115 suppers and
50 snacks per week. Senior Transportation – Our paratransit program continues to provide trips
to seniors and the disabled community in Inglewood and Hawthorne, including vital trips to dialysis
centers.

REPORT - DIRECTOR. Parks, Recreation, and Community Service Department Director Thomas
Uwal reported on the following: Donation to the Wild Fires – We continue to receive inquiries
from residents about donating for the victims of wildfires in Los Angeles. To donate for the cause,
we encourage our residents to organizations like the American Red Cross, California Community
Foundation's Wildfire Recovery Fund, Los Angeles Fire Department Foundation, or World Central
Kitchen. Community Information Guide – The Department is working to put together the
Community Information Guide for Spring/Summer 2025. The upcoming issue will cover April 2025
through September 2025. 2025 Special Events Calendar – The Department completed the 2025
Special Events Annual Calendar. The calendar is sent to Mayor and Council, Commissioners and
City Departments so that they can plan accordingly to attend the scheduled events. Inglewood
Annual Jazz Festival – The 3nd Annual Inglewood Music Festival is scheduled for Saturday, June 28,
2025, at Darby Park. The event celebrates the City’s cultural diversity through variety of music. Last
year’s festival attracted over 4,000 in attendance, and an even larger turnout is expected this

  3
   Park and Recreation Commission

year. The event aims to provide a welcoming environment where residents can sing, dance and
enjoy the community spirit.

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None.

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS. Commissioner Padilla thanked Anthony Harris for the tour of the
city’s Sports website. He suggested taking a tour of the Senior Center with children to include a
program such as poetry reading.

Commissioner Denmon extended his congratulations to Commissioner Brown on his 80th birthday.
He encouraged the Commissioners including, himself to get back out into the community and
attend events to obtain feedback. He also asked for a follow-up on Maliaka Mitchell. Thomas Uwal
stated he met with her and gave her some items needed for the kids and she promised she would
come back to report to the Commission.

There being no further business to be presented, Commissioner Denmon declared the meeting
adjourned at the hour of 6:45 p.m.
